feeds.title: Japanese American National Museum Blog
feeds.description: Japanese American National Museum. They are creating a better understanding of their diverse society by sharing the Japanese American experience through their museum. Explore their blog to know about them, their culture, community, museum functions, feature stories, events and updates.

feeds.title: Portland JACL Blog
feeds.description: Portland JACL is a civil rights advocacy group that strives to educate the public and secure and uphold the human rights of all and promote and preserve the cultural heritage and values of Japanese Americans. Their education blog features posts on laws, policies, Japanese American, government issues, community news and updates.

feeds.title: Japanese American Museum of Oregon Blog
feeds.description: Formerly known as the Oregon Nikkei Legacy Center, the Japanese American Museum of Oregon at Naito Center is a venue for culture and research as well as an invaluable resource for exploring Nikkei experiences and their role in Oregon's multicultural community. Their permanent exhibit space highlights Issei immigration and early life in Oregon, Nihonmachi (Japantown), life after Executive Order 9066 (including the Portland Assembly Center), and contemporary Nikkei life.

feeds.title: Japan-America Society of Dallas/Fort Worth Blog
feeds.description: The Japan-America Society of Dallas was founded in 1970 to promote friendship and understanding between Japanese and Americans in Dallas. The Japan-America Society of Dallas/Fort Worth furthers mutual understanding and ongoing engagement between Japanese and Americans. They provide quality programs in arts and culture, education, business, public policy, and international exchange, and create opportunities for friendship and meaningful interaction. Go through their blog to know more about their society and their progress over the years.

feeds.title: Registers.com
feeds.description: Registers.com blog features The history and literature of Japanese American resistance to wartime incarceration. The site is about the Japanese American resistance to wartime incarceration during World War II. It is a project of the Densho Digital Archive, a non-profit organization that preserves and shares the history of Japanese Americans and Japanese Canadians

feeds.title: Densho
feeds.description: Densho's blog shares Preserve and shares the history of the WWII incarceration of Japanese Americans to promote equity and justice today. Their mission is to Preserve Japanese American stories of the past for the generations of tomorrow.

feeds.title: Just One Cookbook
feeds.description: Just One Cookbook is a Japanese food blog with 1000+ authentic home-style recipes. Learn the cuisine with easy step-by-step photo instructions and videos. Founder of Just One Cookbook Shares easy Japanese recipes with step-by-step photos on the blog and video tutorials on the YouTube channel.

feeds.title: Rafu Shimpo
feeds.description: Handpicked, Accurate, and Relevant stories that provide a birds-eye view of the Little Tokyo community. Read up on Japanese culture, Anime, as well as community and politics. The Rafu Shimpo is the nation's leading Japanese American newspaper since its original publication, proudly serving the Japanese American community from Downtown Los Angeles.

feeds.title: The North American Post
feeds.description: The North American Post has served Seattle's Japanese Community since 1902. Their articles are all about Japanese in Seattle, including Japanese and Japanese American community news, Japanese-related events, Japanese restaurant reviews, Japanese cooking recipes, community interviews, and more.

feeds.title: Pacific Citizen
feeds.description: Published by the JACL the nation's oldest and largest APA civil rights organization, the Pacific Citizen is committed to delivering the most incisive coverage of important APA stories that are often ignored by other media outlets.

feeds.title: National Japanese American Historical Society
feeds.description: The National Japanese American Historical Society, Inc. (NJAHS), is a 501 c (3) non-profit organization, incorporated in 1981, and dedicated to the collection, preservation, authentic interpretation, and sharing of historical information of the Japanese American experience for the diverse broader national and global community.

feeds.title: JapanUp! Magazine
feeds.description: Founded in 2003, JapanUp! The magazine company runs 4 business operations a publishing business (3 magazines), an event business, a production business, and consulting for companies starting new businesses in America. As a team, their staff will do their best to make LALALA the transmitter of valuable information that will assist and enrich Japanese lifestyles in the United States.

feeds.title: Japanese American Association of New York
feeds.description: Since 1907, JAANY has been the heart of the Japanese community. They serve their community through bilingual social services, educational programs, and community outreach. With a strong sense of diversity, they have always been a collaborative forum, celebrating and sharing the Japanese culture and heritage with people of all ages and backgrounds. They are Dedicated to connecting their community through social engagement, education, sports, and the arts.

feeds.title: JACL Honolulu
feeds.description: Founded in 1929, the National JACL is the oldest and largest Asian American civil rights organization in the United States. The JACL monitors and responds to issues that enhance or threaten the civil and human rights of all Americans and implements strategies to effect positive social change, particularly in the Asian-Pacific American community. Their Honolulu chapter shares all the details of their work, activities, events, news and updates.

feeds.title: San Diego JACL
feeds.description: Founded in 1929, the JACL is the oldest and largest Asian American civil rights organization in the United States. They are recognized for their dedication to the Japanese American community by supporting social wellness, providing cultural and educational programs for the youth, promoting communication between local Japanese American organizations, and responding to the needs, concerns, and ideas of the people in the greater San Diego region, who share a common bond of Japanese heritage.

feeds.title: Japanese American Citizens League Arizona Chapter
feeds.description: The JACL chapter in Arizona is the legacy of Japanese immigrants who settled in Arizona territory in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. By the early twentieth century, Japanese American families moved to Arizona and began truck farming small crops for the local market.

feeds.title: JACL Chicago
feeds.description: Founded in 1929, the JACL is the oldest and largest Asian American civil rights organization in the United States. The JACL monitors and responds to issues that enhance or threaten the civil and human rights of all Americans and implements strategies to effect positive social change, particularly to the Asian-Pacific American community. Their Chicago chapter has news section sharing the latest new snap updates form the organization along with some informational articles.

feeds.title: St. Louis JACL
feeds.description: Founded in 1929, the JACL is the oldest and largest Asian American civil rights organization in the United States. The JACL monitors and responds to issues that enhance or threaten the civil and human rights of all Americans and implements strategies to effect positive social change, particularly to the Asian-Pacific American community. The St. Louis Chapter of the JACL has its origins starting in 1946.

feeds.title: Japanese Cooking 101
feeds.description: Japanese Cooking 101 is a website and YouTube channel that teaches people how to cook Japanese food. The blog site was founded by Noriko and Yuko, two Japanese women who are passionate about sharing their love of Japanese cuisine with the world. The blog features over 300 recipes, all of which are accompanied by step-by-step instructions and photos.

feeds.title: Oishii Desu
feeds.description: Est. in Los Angeles on April 2016. Oishii Desu is one of, if not the largest resource for Japanese Food and Culture in the World for English speakers. Oishii Desu is a blog that focuses on Japanese food and culture in the United States and the world. The blog features articles on various topics such as food reviews, restaurant recommendations, interviews with people in the food industry, and information about Japanese condiments

feeds.title: Mochi Mommy
feeds.description: Mochi Mommy is a blog about Asian-inspired recipes and family life. The blog was created by Christina, a mom of two who loves to cook and bake. She shares her recipes for both savory and sweet dishes, as well as tips and tricks for making Asian food at home. The blog also features posts about Christina's family life, including her experiences as a mom of two young children.

feeds.title: Plates by Nat
feeds.description: Find easy and scrumptious recipes with an Asian twist here and there. Everything on Plates by Nat is gluten and dairy free! Blog author Natsuko is a recipe developer, writer, and photographer behind this blog. She creates, curates, and presents healthy, gluten-free dishes and tips for readers to enjoy their meals without being conscious of health.

feeds.title: Maido! Blog
feeds.description: Maido! was founded in 2003 by Seiko Dailey and is the only Japanese-owned grocery store in the Greater Philadelphia area. They opened the first store in Narberth and moved to Ardmore to expand the store. Their blog shares information about their store, their products, their uses, special offers, deals, daily updates, news and more.

feeds.title: Bainbridge Island Japanese American Community Blog (BIJAC)
feeds.description: The Bainbridge Island Japanese American Community (BIJAC) website is dedicated to preserving and sharing the history and culture of Japanese Americans of Bainbridge Island. The site contains a collection of photographs, artifacts, and recorded firsthand accounts that illustrate the human stories behind the exclusion and internment of Japanese Americans during World War II. Their blog section features news and updates about the community, including events, memorials, and grant awards.

feeds.title: Japanese American Museum of San Jose Blog
feeds.description: JAMsj showcases a unique collection of permanent and rotating exhibits chronicling more than a century of Japanese American history. Follow their museum blog for information about Japanese American culture, museum insights, feature stories, news and update.

feeds.title: Japanese American Living in Japan
feeds.description: The Japanese American Living in Japan blog is about a girl who is staying in America and has moved from Japan. In her blog, she showcases her life and her daily activities. shares her past experiences, and an overall guide for an Japanese person who is staying or willing to stay in America.

feeds.title: The New Mexico Japanese-American Citizens League (NMJACL)
feeds.description: The mission of the New Mexico Japanese American Citizens League is to promote, protect, and fight for the civil and human rights of ALL PEOPLE in and outside of New Mexico. The NMJACL recognizes the importance of education and, following New Mexico's multicultural traditions, promotes the awareness of the Japanese culture in the community. The NMJACL actively works with the community to promote the brother/sisterhood of all cultures in New Mexico.

feeds.title: JACL Philadelphia
feeds.description: The Japanese Cultural Activities Resource Guidecontains a number of activities suitable for youth between the ages of 5 and 12 years. The main goal is to offer resources through which multi- and bi-racial youth can explore their Japanese heritage. This 59-page book is made possible by the JACL Legacy Fund Grants Program. This guide was written by the Sonoma (Calif) County Taiko & Japanese Cultural Camp Committee.

feeds.title: San Francisco JACL
feeds.description: Founded in 1929, the Japanese American Citizens League is the oldest and largest Asian American civil rights organization in the United States. The JACL champions issues affecting the Japanese American and Asian-Pacific-American communities and advocates for the civil and human rights of all Americans. The San Francisco Chapter has a storied history as one of the earliest to be formed and has been the home chapter to many national JACL leaders.

feeds.title: The Japanese Kitchen
feeds.description: A Japanese food blog by Tanpopo Journeys. Browse our favorite recipes that you can make and share with friends and family. Healthy, easy, and delicious! Their passion is to takes us to Japan to see where and how food is prepared and to fully experience their culture and food.

feeds.title: Tofugu
feeds.description: Tofugu is a website and blog about Japanese culture and language. It was founded in 2007 by Matt Alt, a Japanese-American writer and translator. The site has since grown to become one of the most popular resources for information about Japan, with over 10 million monthly visitors. Tofugu covers a wide range of topics related to Japan, including language learning, culture, food, travel, and pop culture

feeds.title: The JBeauty Collection Blog
feeds.description: The J-Beauty Collection blog is your guide to the J-Beauty skincare routine, the latest trends, cult-favorite brands, and breakthrough skincare technology from the wondrous world of Japanese beauty. They are a curated site committed to introducing products exclusively from Japan.

feeds.title: JapanAmerica
feeds.description: Japanamerica is a blog about the book Japanamerica how Japanese pop culture has invaded the US by Japanese american author Roland.
